extracted.intended_audience: regulatory professionals, engaged public/commenters, and civic-technology practitioners interested in federal rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for people who comment on federal rulemakings and for those improving the Regulations.gov platform; covers platform usability problems, recommended platform features, and practical steps commenters should take (cross-docket search, demand RIAs, cross-check Reginfo.gov).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistent, user-friendly document categorization
rubrics_metrics.description: Search Difficulties — document categorization is 'unusual and confusing'; document types like 'advance notices of proposed rulemaking' are inconsistently labeled across agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use consistent, comprehensible labels for document types across agencies; involve users in labeling decisions so search filters and categories match how people look for materials. Anti-pattern: agency-specific or inconsistent type names that frustrate search and discovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linking and consolidating related dockets
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple Dockets Problem — agencies create separate dockets for the same rulemaking without linking them; a sub-agency might propose in one docket while the parent finalizes in another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide mechanisms to identify, link, and consolidate dockets that pertain to the same regulatory action to prevent fragmentation of materials and comments. Automated suggestions or admin workflows should surface related dockets for consolidation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide supporting materials and contextual documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Missing Context — many dockets 'lack important context'; some have no supporting materials despite inviting comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure dockets include the studies, background documents, and regulatory impact analyses that agencies relied upon. At minimum, link or upload RIAs, studies, and supporting evidence so commenters can review the underlying basis for the proposal. Anti-pattern: inviting comments while withholding the analytic documents commenters need to provide informed responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make rulemaking status and cross-system metadata visible
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Long-term action' status often appears only on Reginfo.gov and not on Regulations.gov, obscuring the true status and history of actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expose status indicators and relevant metadata (e.g., long-term action, stages of rulemaking) within the platform so users can understand where a rule stands without consulting separate systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: User-centered design for platform improvements
rubrics_metrics.description: User-Centered Design — involve actual users in labeling decisions; adopt 'agile approaches' consistent with the U.S. Digital Service playbook.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design interfaces, taxonomies, and workflows based on observed user needs and iterative testing. Employ agile development and usability testing with real commenters, agency staff, and other stakeholders to prioritize fixes that materially improve discoverability and participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automated alert and suggestion system for related dockets
rubrics_metrics.description: Automated Alert System — back-end alerts prompting agency managers when creating new dockets, suggesting related dockets and enabling consolidation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement backend tooling that detects potentially related dockets (by topic, citation, agency, or identifiers) and alerts managers to link or merge them. Guidance should include prompts to consolidate rather than proliferate redundant dockets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-database interoperability (Reginfo.gov integration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cross-Database Integration — interoperability with Reginfo.gov and other rulemaking databases is needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build APIs and data-exchange links so Regulations.gov can surface information maintained in other federal rulemaking repositories (e.g., Reginfo.gov), reducing the need for users to search multiple systems. Prioritize synchronizing key metadata and status fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commenter due diligence: search across multiple dockets
rubrics_metrics.description: Implication for Commenters — commenters must work harder than the platform suggests: search across multiple dockets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing comments, manually search for related dockets, affiliated rulemakings, and past dockets that may bear on the issue. Do not assume one docket contains all relevant documents or comments; check agency sites and cross-references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commenter due diligence: cross-check Reginfo.gov
rubrics_metrics.description: Implication for Commenters — commenters should cross-check Reginfo.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify rule status, long-term action listings, and other metadata on Reginfo.gov and reconcile with what's posted on Regulations.gov. Use Reginfo.gov to uncover actions or context that may not be visible on Regulations.gov.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commenter practice: demand agencies' analytic documents before drafting
rubrics_metrics.description: Implication for Commenters — demand the agency's underlying analytic documents (RIA, studies) before drafting; 'Citizens cannot submit quality comments without reviewing studies and background documents underlying proposed regulations.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require and reference the agency's regulatory impact analyses, studies, and supporting evidence in your comments. If such documents are not available in the docket, request them from the agency or cite their absence as a substantive issue in your comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle: meaningful participation requires access to well-informed views and relevant information
rubrics_metrics.description: Meaningful public engagement demands access to 'well-informed views and relevant information' the agency relied upon during development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat access to agency reasoning and evidence as a prerequisite for legitimate public participation; both platform designers and agencies should prioritize transparency to enable informed public input. Commenters should base comments on that information to be substantive and useful.
